title: annex/v2
description: The front matter of nodes/<id>/annex/<hash>.md (D-31): an informal argument attached to a node as input, never as a claim. The file is markdown whose head is a YAML block delimited by --- lines carrying these fields; the rest is prose, served as demarcated untrusted data (D-28) and read by nothing in the network for truth. The file name is the SHA-256 of the whole file, so the citation a skeleton makes (D-31) is mechanical and an edit is a new annex. licence is required because D-23's amendment accepts annex prose only when its author licenses it at submission. An annex earns nothing on submission and nothing later (D-31), so there is no credit field. annex/v2 (D-31 v3.26, stepped outlines) adds optional steps: the outline's steps, each an identifier and a one-line summary. A skeleton that cites a stepped annex names each hole after one of its steps, and the gate refuses one that does not (annex-step-missing, at the end of step 4, where the extractor has named the holes); a step with no hole is carried by the assembly. A step id is ASCII, a letter or underscore then letters, digits, underscores or primes, so it is a Lean identifier a `have` can bind as written; ids are unique within the annex, which the gate and the service check beside this schema. A summary is untrusted contributor data (C9, D-28): shown, escaped, never read for truth.

contributor.description: The submitting identity's pseudonym; set by the service, never by the caller

licence.description: SPDX identifier the author licenses this prose under (D-23 amendment)

model_and_tooling.description: What drafted the prose, as declared (D-23); null when a human wrote it

steps.description: The outline's steps in the annex's order (D-31 v3.26). Ids are unique within the list.

id.description: The name a skeleton's hole for this step binds: `have <id> : … := sorry`. ASCII only.

summary.description: One line saying what the step establishes; untrusted data, shown escaped (C9)
